plan_info.primary_goal: Increase total-body strength to support half-marathon training, improve core stability, enhance running economy, and maintain flexibility with a gym-friendly 5-day plan.
safety_notes: Low risk and cleared for exercise; still stop immediately for chest pain, unusual shortness of breath, dizziness/fainting, new palpitations, or severe headache.
Pain rule: 0–2/10 acceptable; 3–4/10 modify (reduce load/range/speed); 5+/10 or sharp/nerve pain = stop and reassess.
Warm up 5–10 minutes before strength or running; ramp intensity gradually (no sudden speed/load jumps).
Maintain neutral spine for hinges/squats/rows; avoid breath-holding—exhale on effort, inhale on lowering.
Progress gradually: change only ONE variable at a time (load OR reps OR sets OR running intensity) weekly, and only if recovery is good.
Use stable, non-slip surfaces for step-ups/lunges; use wall support only for balance, not to pull.
For resistance bands, anchor securely and inspect for wear/tears before use to prevent snapping.
Hydrate and fuel appropriately; avoid high-intensity sessions if ill, feverish, or significantly sleep-deprived.

weekly_schedule.focus: 5-Day Strength + Run Support Block (2 lower-focused days, 1 upper-focused day, 2 run-quality/core days)

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.description: Builds quad/glute strength and trunk bracing to support running posture and power.
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out; hold one dumbbell at chest with elbows down.
Brace core (ribs down). Inhale and sit hips back and down as knees track over 2nd–3rd toes.
Lower to a comfortable depth with neutral spine (stop before back rounds).
Exhale and drive through midfoot/heel to stand tall; squeeze glutes at the top.
tips: Keep chest tall and weight close to the body.
Maintain tripod foot contact (big toe, little toe, heel).
Avoid knees collapsing inward; push knees slightly out.
exercises.easier: Bodyweight squat to a box/bench (sit lightly then stand).
exercises.harder: Add a 2-second pause at the bottom or increase load slightly with perfect form.
warnings: Stop if sharp knee pain occurs or pain worsens during the set.
Avoid rounding the lower back at the bottom.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
exercises.description: Strengthens hamstrings/glutes and teaches hip hinge mechanics for stride power and posterior-chain resilience.
steps: Stand holding two dumbbells in front of thighs; feet hip-width; knees softly bent.
Brace core and push hips back while keeping dumbbells close to legs.
Lower until strong hamstring stretch (stop before spine rounds).
Exhale and drive hips forward to stand tall; squeeze glutes at the top.
tips: Think 'hips back' (hinge), not 'bend at the waist'.
Keep neck neutral; shoulders packed down and back.
Control the lowering phase; no bouncing.
exercises.easier: Reduce range of motion to just below knees and use lighter weights.
exercises.harder: Use a 3-second slow lowering phase (eccentric) while keeping form.
warnings: Stop for sharp low-back pain, tingling, or numbness.
Do not lock knees or hyperextend at the top.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
exercises.description: Builds single-leg strength and hip control with typically less forward knee stress than forward lunges.
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width; brace core.
Step one foot back and lower until both knees bend ~90° (back knee hovers above floor).
Keep front knee tracking over toes; chest tall.
Press through front heel to return to standing; repeat then switch sides.
tips: Step back far enough to keep front shin relatively vertical.
Control the descent (2–3 seconds down).
Keep hips level; avoid wobbling.
exercises.easier: Shorten the step length and reduce depth; use wall support for balance.
exercises.harder: Hold light dumbbells or add a 1-second pause at the bottom.
warnings: Stop if sharp knee pain occurs; reduce depth or switch to split squat hold.
Avoid letting the front knee cave inward.

exercises.name: Step-Up
exercises.description: Improves unilateral leg strength and hip stability; supports better knee tracking for running.
steps: Stand facing a sturdy step/box; place whole foot on the step.
Drive through the step foot to stand up (minimal push from trailing foot).
Stand tall at the top; bring trailing foot up.
Step down under control; complete reps then switch legs.
tips: Keep knee aligned over 2nd–3rd toes; avoid collapsing inward.
Use a step height at or below knee height to start.
Control the lowering phase to build stability.
exercises.easier: Lower step height and perform bodyweight only.
exercises.harder: Hold light dumbbells or use a slow 3-second lowering phase.
warnings: Ensure the step is stable and non-slip.
Stop if sharp knee pain occurs.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
exercises.description: Builds calf/Achilles capacity for propulsion and lower-leg injury prevention in runners.
steps: Stand near a wall for light fingertip support; shift weight to one foot.
Rise up slowly onto the ball of the foot (about 2 seconds up).
Pause briefly at the top, then lower slowly (about 3 seconds down).
Complete reps and switch legs.
tips: Keep knee straight but not locked for gastrocnemius emphasis.
No bouncing; control every rep.
Keep hips level; avoid leaning.
exercises.easier: Double-leg calf raises or smaller range on flat ground.
exercises.harder: Perform on a step for more range or hold a light dumbbell.
warnings: Stop if Achilles pain becomes sharp or increases.
Avoid fast, bouncing reps.

exercises.name: Treadmill Interval Run (1:2 Work:Rest)
exercises.description: Builds speed endurance and aerobic power while keeping effort controlled.
steps: Warm up 8 minutes easy jog (RPE 3/10).
Complete 6 rounds: 1 minute hard (RPE 8/10) + 2 minutes easy (RPE 3/10).
Cool down 5 minutes easy jog or brisk walk.
Optional: set treadmill incline to 1% for outdoor-like effort.
tips: Hard segments should be challenging but repeatable—avoid sprinting.
Keep cadence quick and steps light (avoid overstriding).
If form breaks, reduce speed during hard segments.
exercises.easier: Do 4 rounds or use 45 seconds hard / 2 minutes easy.
exercises.harder: Increase to 7–8 rounds or add 1–2% incline on hard segments.
warnings: Stop for dizziness, chest pain, or unusual shortness of breath.
Stop for sharp joint pain; reduce speed or switch to low-impact cardio.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.description: Improves trunk and hip stability, supporting spinal control and balanced gait.
steps: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Brace core and keep back flat; avoid shifting weight.
Extend opposite arm and leg to parallel; keep hips square.
Return with control and alternate sides.
tips: Reach long (not high) to avoid low-back arching.
Move slowly and breathe steadily.
Keep gaze down to maintain neutral neck.
exercises.easier: Extend only the leg or only the arm (one limb at a time).
exercises.harder: Add a 2-second hold at full extension each rep.
warnings: Stop if low-back pinching occurs; reduce range and re-brace.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.description: Trains deep core stability to reduce low-back stress during running and lifting.
steps: Lie on your back; hips/knees at 90°, arms up.
Press low back gently into the floor; ribs down.
Extend opposite arm and leg slowly without back lifting.
Return to start and switch sides.
tips: Exhale during extension to keep ribs down.
Reduce range if low back lifts.
Slow, controlled reps > speed.
exercises.easier: Heel taps only with arms still.
exercises.harder: Add a brief 1–2 second pause at end range each rep.
warnings: Stop if you feel low-back pain; decrease range and re-brace.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.description: Strengthens lateral core/hip stabilizers to reduce pelvic drop and improve running efficiency.
steps: Lie on your side with elbow under shoulder; legs stacked or staggered.
Lift hips to form a straight line from head to feet.
Keep ribs down and glutes engaged; breathe steadily.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep shoulders stacked; don’t roll forward.
Squeeze glutes to stabilize hips.
Stop before form breaks.
exercises.easier: Side plank from knees (bent legs).
exercises.harder: Increase hold to 35–40 seconds or add a small top-leg lift.
warnings: Stop if shoulder pain increases; regress to knees.

exercises.name: Pallof Press (Resistance Band)
exercises.description: Anti-rotation core strength to stabilize trunk during running and lifting.
steps: Anchor band at chest height; stand sideways with feet shoulder-width.
Hold band at chest with both hands; step out to create tension.
Brace core and press hands straight out without rotating.
Return to chest with control; complete reps then switch sides.
tips: Squeeze glutes and keep ribs down.
Move slowly; resist band pull.
Keep knees soft and posture tall.
exercises.easier: Stand closer to anchor (less tension).
exercises.harder: Add a 2-second hold with arms extended each rep.
warnings: Stop if you feel twisting low-back discomfort; reduce tension.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.description: Builds chest/shoulder/triceps strength and trunk stiffness for posture and arm drive.
steps: Start in a high plank: hands under shoulders, core braced, glutes tight.
Lower under control; elbows 30–45° from body; chest approaches floor.
Keep body in a straight line (no sagging hips).
Exhale and press back up.
tips: Keep shoulders away from ears.
Hands can be slightly wider than shoulders if comfortable.
Maintain strong plank throughout.
exercises.easier: Incline push-up on a bench or wall.
exercises.harder: Slow 3-second lowering or add a 1-second pause at the bottom.
warnings: Stop for sharp shoulder pain; regress to incline and reduce depth.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
exercises.description: Strengthens lats/upper back for shoulder health and upright posture.
steps: Stand hip-width holding dumbbells; hinge to ~45° with flat back.
Brace core; let arms hang under shoulders.
Row elbows toward lower ribs; squeeze shoulder blades.
Lower with control and repeat.
tips: Lead with elbows; avoid shrugging.
No swinging; pause briefly at top.
Keep neck neutral.
exercises.easier: Single-arm supported row with one hand on a bench.
exercises.harder: Add a 1-second pause at the top each rep or increase load slightly.
warnings: Stop if low-back discomfort increases; support on a bench and reduce load.

exercises.name: Band Pull-Apart
exercises.description: Improves scapular control and posture by activating rear delts/rhomboids.
steps: Stand tall; hold band at shoulder height with arms straight (soft elbows).
Pull band apart by squeezing shoulder blades back and down.
Pause briefly at end range.
Return slowly while keeping tension.
tips: Don’t shrug; shoulders down.
Keep ribs stacked (avoid arching low back).
Control the return—no snapping.
exercises.easier: Use a lighter band or reduce range of motion.
exercises.harder: Add a 2-second hold at end range each rep.
warnings: Stop if shoulder pinching occurs; reduce range and set scapula down/back.

exercises.name: Band External Rotation (Elbow at Side)
exercises.description: Strengthens rotator cuff for shoulder stability and injury prevention.
steps: Anchor band at elbow height; stand sideways to anchor.
Keep elbow pinned at side at 90°; towel between elbow and ribs if needed.
Rotate forearm outward without moving elbow or twisting torso.
Return slowly with control.
tips: Use light resistance; prioritize control.
Keep shoulder blade gently down/back.
Move only at the shoulder.
exercises.easier: Use a lighter band and smaller range.
exercises.harder: Add a 2-second pause at end range each rep.
warnings: Stop if pain/catching increases; reduce tension and range.

exercises.name: Front Plank (Forearm)
exercises.description: Builds core endurance for stable posture and efficient breathing during longer runs.
steps: Place forearms on floor with elbows under shoulders; legs extended.
Brace core (ribs down) and squeeze glutes to form a straight line.
Hold while breathing slowly; stop before form breaks.
Rest and repeat.
tips: Push the floor away to stabilize shoulders.
Don’t let hips sag or pike.
Keep neck neutral.
exercises.easier: Knee plank with the same bracing cues.
exercises.harder: Increase hold to 45 seconds or add shoulder taps with strict control.
warnings: Stop if low-back pain occurs; reset with stronger glute squeeze and shorter holds.

exercises.name: Dynamic Warm-Up (Run Prep)
exercises.description: Prepares joints/tissues for impact and improves stride mechanics before tempo work.
steps: Easy jog or brisk walk 5 minutes.
Leg swings front/back: 10 per leg (hold wall).
Leg swings side-to-side: 10 per leg (control pelvis).
Walking lunges: 10 total (5 each side) with tall posture.
2 x 20-second relaxed strides with 40 seconds easy between (optional).
tips: Keep movements controlled—no ballistic swinging.
Build intensity gradually.
Stay tall and relaxed through shoulders.
exercises.easier: Skip strides and keep warm-up to brisk walk + leg swings only.
exercises.harder: Add one extra stride (3 total) if feeling great.
warnings: If any joint pain appears during warm-up, reduce range/intensity immediately.

exercises.name: Tempo Run (Comfortably Hard)
exercises.description: Builds sustained speed endurance (threshold) needed for half-marathon pacing.
steps: After warm-up, run 12 minutes at comfortably hard effort (RPE ~7/10).
You should be able to speak short phrases but not hold a full conversation.
Finish with 5–8 minutes easy jog/walk cooldown.
tips: Hold steady effort; don’t turn it into a race.
Relax shoulders, keep cadence smooth.
If effort creeps too high, slow slightly and stay controlled.
exercises.easier: 2 x 6 minutes tempo with 2 minutes easy between.
exercises.harder: Increase tempo to 15 minutes if recovery is excellent.
warnings: Stop for dizziness, chest pain, or unusual shortness of breath.
Avoid pushing pace if legs feel heavy from earlier sessions.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge / Hip Thrust (Bodyweight)
exercises.description: Strengthens glutes/hamstrings to support hip extension power and reduce compensations in running.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat hip-width.
Brace core and squeeze glutes to lift hips until shoulders–hips–knees align.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower slowly with control.
Repeat without letting knees flare excessively.
tips: Drive through heels and keep ribs down (avoid back arching).
Squeeze glutes at the top; don’t push with low back.
Keep knees tracking over toes.
exercises.easier: Reduce range of motion or perform 2 sets of 10.
exercises.harder: Single-leg glute bridge (alternate legs) or add a 2–3 second hold at top.
warnings: Stop if you feel sharp low-back pain; reset with stronger core brace and smaller range.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.description: Maintains hip extension range to support stride length and reduce anterior hip tightness post-run.
steps: Kneel on one knee with the other foot forward (lunge stance).
Tuck pelvis slightly (posterior pelvic tilt) and squeeze the back-side glute.
Gently shift forward until you feel a stretch in the front of the hip.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Keep torso tall; don’t arch low back.
Squeeze glute on the kneeling side for a better stretch.
Breathe slowly and relax into the hold.
exercises.easier: Shorten hold to 20 seconds and reduce forward shift.
exercises.harder: Raise the same-side arm overhead and slightly side-bend away (gentle).
warnings: Stop if you feel pinching in the front of the hip; reduce range.

exercises.name: Hamstring Stretch (Hip Hinge Hold)
exercises.description: Maintains posterior chain flexibility and reduces post-run stiffness.
steps: Stand tall and place one heel slightly forward with toes up.
Hinge at hips with a flat back until you feel a mild hamstring stretch.
Keep knee softly straight (not locked).
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Hinge from hips, not rounding the spine.
Keep shoulders relaxed and breathe.
Stretch to mild discomfort only.
exercises.easier: Decrease hinge depth and hold for 20 seconds.
exercises.harder: Increase hold to 40 seconds if comfortable.
warnings: Stop if sharp pain occurs; do not bounce.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat (Moderate Volume)
exercises.description: Reinforces squat pattern and leg strength endurance for overall athletic capacity.
steps: Set up as Day 1.
Use a moderate load you can control for all reps.
Keep knees tracking and spine neutral.
Stand tall and reset breath each rep.
tips: Quality reps only; stop 1–2 reps before form breaks.
Keep ribs down and weight close.
exercises.easier: Bodyweight squat 3x12.
exercises.harder: Add a 1-second pause at the bottom each rep.
warnings: Avoid knee collapse and low-back rounding.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge / Hip Thrust (Bodyweight)
exercises.description: Strengthens glutes for hip extension power and pelvic control in running.
steps: Lie on back, knees bent, feet flat hip-width.
Brace core and lift hips by squeezing glutes.
Pause briefly at the top; lower slowly.
Repeat with controlled tempo.
tips: Drive through heels; keep ribs down.
Avoid flaring ribs or arching low back.
Keep knees aligned over toes.
exercises.easier: 2 sets of 10 with smaller range.
exercises.harder: Single-leg glute bridge (8 reps each side) or 2–3 second top hold.
warnings: Stop if low-back pain increases; reset brace and reduce range.

exercises.name: Step-Up
exercises.description: Single-leg strength and stability to support balanced mechanics and reduce asymmetries.
steps: Use a sturdy step; place whole foot on top.
Drive through step foot to stand; minimal push from trailing foot.
Stand tall at top; step down slowly.
Complete reps and switch sides.
tips: Control the lowering phase.
Keep knee aligned; pelvis level.
Use wall support lightly if needed.
exercises.easier: Lower step height and do bodyweight only.
exercises.harder: Hold dumbbells or add a 3-second descent.
warnings: Stop if sharp knee pain occurs.
Ensure step is stable and non-slip.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row
exercises.description: Builds back strength and postural endurance; supports shoulder health for lifting/yoga.
steps: Hinge forward with flat back; brace core.
Row elbows toward lower ribs; squeeze shoulder blades.
Lower with control and repeat.
Keep neck neutral throughout.
tips: No swinging; pause briefly at top.
Keep shoulders down (avoid shrugging).
Feel back muscles working.
exercises.easier: Single-arm supported row on a bench.
exercises.harder: Add a 1-second top pause each rep or slightly increase load.
warnings: Stop if low-back discomfort increases; reduce load or support on a bench.

exercises.name: Pallof Press (Resistance Band)
exercises.description: Reinforces anti-rotation control for trunk stability and efficient force transfer.
steps: Anchor band at chest height; stand sideways with feet shoulder-width.
Hold band at chest; step away to create tension.
Press straight out, pause briefly, return slowly.
Complete reps then switch sides.
tips: Squeeze glutes; ribs down.
No rotation—move straight forward.
Keep breathing steady.
exercises.easier: Reduce band tension by standing closer.
exercises.harder: Add a 2-second hold at full extension each rep.
warnings: Stop if twisting low-back discomfort occurs; reduce tension and re-brace.
